::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Simple Surface Integral problem](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2517468/simple-surface-integral-problem), asked by [sksumii13](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/502257/sksumii13) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-11-12; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Hi here's the question I am working on:
>
> Calculate the surface integral of $F \cdot dS$: $F(x,y,z) = (2x, 2y, 2z)$
>
> $S$ is the side of the cylinder $x^2 + y^2 = 9$ and $0 < z < 5$ , without top and bottom, oriented outwards.
>
> I parametrized $S$ using $r(\theta,z) = (3\cdot\cos(\theta), 3\cdot\sin(\theta),z)$
> and found $F \cdot (r_\theta\times r_z)$ is $18$.
>
> Thus I have $18(5)(2\pi) = 180\pi$  
>
> but I have a different answer from the teacher.  
>
> Any insights as to what I did wrong?
:::

I think you forgot that the radius of the cylinder was $3$, not $1$.

You don't really need a parametrization, but if you use one, you should get that
$$\mathbf{n}(x,y,z) = \frac{1}{3}\left<x,y,0\right>$$
Therefore 
$$\mathbf{F} \cdot\mathbf{n} = \left<2x,2y,2z\right> \cdot \frac{1}{3}\left<x,y,0\right> = \frac{2}{3}(x^2 + y^2) = 6$$
(not $18$, as you have).  So
$$\iint_S \mathbf{F}\cdot d\mathbf{S} = \iint_S \mathbf{F}\cdot\mathbf{n}\,dS = 6 \cdot\operatorname{Area}(S) = 6 \cdot 5\cdot 6\pi = 180\pi$$
(again, the circumference is $6\pi$, not $2\pi$).
